title: wall-snmpinfo output
description: Reads identity, uptime and printer supply levels from one device over SNMP. Usage: wall-snmpinfo IP [--snmp-version 2c] [--port 161] [--timeout-ms MS] [--retries N]. The community string comes from the WALL_SNMP_COMMUNITY environment variable, not the command line (other users can read command lines in the process list), and never appears in the output.

status.description: ok: finished with no errors. partial: finished, result present but incomplete (see errors). error: failed, result is null.

result.description: Tool-specific payload; null when status is error.

allOf.$comment: partial -> at least one error, result present
error -> at least one error, result is null

schema_version.description: Contract version, MAJOR.MINOR. This file is the contract for major version 1: every 1.x document must validate against it.

name.description: Program that produced the document, e.g. "wall-scan".

version.description: Package version of that program (its git tag without the leading v). Independent of schema_version.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time in UTC with a Z suffix, e.g. "2026-10-08T09:30:00Z". Fractional seconds allowed.

code.description: Machine-readable snake_case code. Open set: new codes may appear in any minor version, so consumers must handle codes they do not know.

message.description: Human-readable explanation, safe to show in the UI.

target.description: The input (usually an IP address) this error is about, or null for an error affecting the whole run.

text.description: An SNMP OCTET STRING decoded as UTF-8 (invalid bytes replaced), with trailing NUL bytes and whitespace removed. null when the object is missing or empty.

params.description: The inputs of this run. Credentials (community string, SNMPv3 keys) are deliberately absent.

port.description: UDP port of the SNMP agent, normally 161.

snmp_version.description: SNMP protocol version. Version 3 is listed now so that supporting it later is not a breaking change.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for each SNMP response, in milliseconds.

retries.description: Resends after a timeout, per request.

model.description: Device model: ENTITY-MIB entPhysicalModelName (switches, routers) or, for printers, HOST-RESOURCES-MIB hrDeviceDescr of the printer device. null if the device reports neither.

serial_number.description: Printer-MIB prtGeneralSerialNumber (printers) or ENTITY-MIB entPhysicalSerialNum (switches, routers). null if the device reports neither.

supplies.description: Printer-MIB prtMarkerSuppliesTable, sorted by index. null = the device does not implement Printer-MIB (not a printer), or reading the table failed (status is then partial and errors says so). [] = the device implements it but lists no supplies.

system.description: MIB-II system group (1.3.6.1.2.1.1), which every SNMP agent implements.

descr.description: sysDescr.0: free-text description, often including model and firmware.

object_id.description: sysObjectID.0 in dotted form. The number after 1.3.6.1.4.1 is the vendor's IANA enterprise number (11 = HP, 9 = Cisco).

uptime_s.description: sysUpTime.0 converted from hundredths of a second to whole seconds. This is the SNMP agent's uptime, normally the same as the device's on printers and switches. The counter wraps after about 497 days.

index.description: prtMarkerSuppliesIndex. Stable per slot, so it identifies the same supply across runs.

type.description: prtMarkerSuppliesType as a snake_case name, e.g. toner_cartridge, toner, waste_toner, ink_cartridge, opc, fuser. Unrecognised codes appear as code_<n>. Open set.

colorant.description: prtMarkerColorantValue of this supply's colorant, e.g. black, cyan. null for supplies with no colour (drums, fusers, waste containers).

level_state.description: Decoded from prtMarkerSuppliesLevel per RFC 3805: measured (value >= 0), other (-1), unknown (-2), some_remaining (-3). Closed set, fixed by the RFC.

level.description: prtMarkerSuppliesLevel when level_state is measured, otherwise null. The unit varies by device: often percent, sometimes pages or tenths of grams.

max_capacity.description: prtMarkerSuppliesMaxCapacity, in the same unit as level. null when the device reports -1, -2 or 0.

percent.description: round(100 * level / max_capacity), capped at 100. null unless both level and max_capacity are known. Use this for display and low-toner alerts.

allOf.$comment: level and percent exist only for measured supplies
